must_fix: Do not present the pooled Wilcoxon p-values as if n=60 independent replicates supported the claim. The pool mixes 4 datasets, 3 models, and 5 seeds; observations sharing a dataset/seed and observations from different models are dependent, while the signed-rank test also needs a defensible common, approximately symmetric difference distribution. The current abstract and headline table overstate what p=2.2e-10 establishes.

Explicitly disclose that stats_tests.json contains 20 one-sided tests (4 pooled plus 16 dataset-by-calibrator tests) with no multiple-testing control, and do not treat the resulting p-values as confirmatory across that family.

Remove the statement that the breast-cancer HGB mean-plus/minus-SD 'interval includes 0.' The reported 0.002 plus/minus 0.009 is a descriptive mean plus/minus seed SD, not an uncertainty interval for the effect. Likewise, label pooled SD as heterogeneity/spread rather than uncertainty of the pooled mean.

Close numeric provenance gaps. NumNSeeds and NumAlpha are hard-coded in make_paper_numbers.py rather than read from the two result JSON files, and main.tex contains raw methodological numbers absent from those JSONs (100 trees, 15 ECE bins, 50/25/25 split, and explicit feature/seed indices). These are fabrication-risk under the stated JSON-backed-number policy even though no contradiction was found.
weaknesses: The per-dataset Wilcoxon tests still pool 3 models times 5 seeds (n=15), so they do not resolve the dependence or model heterogeneity in the headline analysis.

One-sided alternatives are used throughout without a documented multiplicity family or a statistical justification for treating the highly heterogeneous, skewed pooled differences as a signed-rank sample from one distribution.
Five seeds satisfy the requested minimum, but n=5 gives only a coarse view of seed variability; the text reports no confidence intervals and sometimes uses SD as if it were inferential.
The abstract's sole p-value is NumNonePooledP, but its placement after claims about all three calibrated conditions can make its scope ambiguous.
strengths: The study uses five seeds, reports seed SDs, sign counts, failures, and an explicit exception rather than claiming universality.
The JSON values support the substantive abstract claims, and the abstract stays within the claims allowed by analysis.md.

All result-derived macros checked against summary_main.json and stats_tests.json round correctly, including pooled means/SDs, sign counts, p-values, cell examples, coverage, and shifted-accuracy values.
The paper openly acknowledges heterogeneous pooling, reports per-dataset results, and distinguishes descriptive help/harm from a calibrator ranking.
